name: United States
genZNote: 50 states, 1 Constitution older than most countries' entire existence, 3 branches of government that are SUPPOSED to check each other — separation of powers, the origin story.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: A federal republic in North America comprising 50 states plus Washington, D.C. (the federal capital district); Alaska and Hawaii are non-contiguous states.
Spans a huge range of geography: Rocky Mountains, Great Plains, Mississippi River system, and coastlines on both the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.
Major cities: Washington, D.C. (capital), New York City (largest city, financial hub), Los Angeles, Chicago.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: English is the dominant language (no official federal language); the country is highly multicultural, built substantially through immigration.
Home to Hollywood (Los Angeles), a globally dominant film and entertainment industry, and Silicon Valley's technology culture.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A federal presidential constitutional republic under the US Constitution (1787, the world's oldest still-functioning written national constitution).
Three-branch separation of powers: Executive (President), Legislative (bicameral Congress — Senate + House of Representatives), Judicial (Supreme Court).
50 states each retain significant autonomy under the federal system.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: Home to NASA, a pioneer of crewed spaceflight (Apollo Moon landings) and major current space exploration programmes.
Leading centre for biomedical research (e.g. NIH) and a major hub for pharmaceutical and biotechnology innovation.
Silicon Valley is a global centre for computing, internet, and AI research and development.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A founding member of the United Nations and NATO; hosts UN Headquarters in New York City.
Member of the G7 and G20; a Quad member alongside India, Japan, and Australia.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: Often described as a 'Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership' — covering defence, trade, technology, and education cooperation.
The US is one of India's largest trading partners, and hosts a very large Indian-American diaspora, prominent in technology and academia.
Both are Quad members alongside Japan and Australia, cooperating on Indo-Pacific security and other shared priorities.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: The world's largest economy by nominal GDP, with services, technology, finance, and manufacturing as major sectors.
The US Dollar is the world's primary reserve currency, used widely in international trade and finance.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Hollywood, Silicon Valley, NASA's space programme, and being the world's largest economy.
The Statue of Liberty, the Grand Canyon, and a federal constitutional system widely studied as a model of separation of powers.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: US Dollar (USD), the world's primary reserve currency.
The world's largest economy by nominal GDP, with strengths spanning technology, finance, agriculture, and manufacturing.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Vast ecological diversity, from Arctic Alaska to subtropical Florida.
Yellowstone, established in 1872, was the world's first national park; the US maintains an extensive National Park System.
Significant biodiversity across its varied climate zones, from deserts to temperate rainforest.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: British colonization began in the early 1600s along the Atlantic coast.
Independence was declared in 1776 following the Revolutionary War.
Westward expansion and the Civil War (1861-1865), which ended slavery, shaped the 19th-century nation; emerged as a global superpower after World War II.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1776 Declaration of Independence formally broke from British rule.
The 1787 Constitution, in effect since 1789, established a federal presidential republic with a system of checks and balances.
27 constitutional amendments have followed, including the abolition of slavery (13th Amendment, 1865) and women's suffrage (19th Amendment, 1920).

sections.heading: 🚀 Space, Innovation & Modern Development
bullets: NASA led the Apollo Moon-landing programme, achieving the first crewed lunar landing in 1969, and continues exploration through the Artemis programme.
A global leader in technology innovation, centred on Silicon Valley, and in private spaceflight through companies such as SpaceX.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: American football, basketball, and baseball are the most popular national sports.
Hollywood is a globally dominant centre of film and entertainment production.
The Statue of Liberty and Grand Canyon are among its most iconic landmarks; has hosted the Olympic Games multiple times.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: A permanent member of the UN Security Council, which is headquartered in New York City.
Founding member of NATO; member of the G7 and G20.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The United States is a federal presidential constitutional republic of 50 states in North America, the world's largest economy by nominal GDP.
keyFacts: Capital: Washington, D.C. Currency: US Dollar.
Constitution: 1787, the world's oldest still-functioning written national constitution.
Three branches: Executive (President), Legislative (Congress), Judicial (Supreme Court).
Quad member alongside India, Japan, and Australia.
commonConfusion: New York City is the LARGEST US city and financial hub, but Washington, D.C. is the CAPITAL — a commonly mixed-up pair.

highYieldFacts: US Constitution (1787) is the world's oldest still-functioning written national constitution.
Three-branch separation of powers: Executive, Legislative, Judicial.
commonTraps: Naming New York City as the US capital instead of Washington, D.C.
mustRemember: US = federal republic, 50 states, Quad member with India, Japan, Australia.
